prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: one transparent pixel-art RPG newspaper kiosk with its resident visible INSIDE the counter; game-ready isolated object.
The reference is the Lume street, for perspective and craftsmanship ONLY. Design a new kiosk for the empty LOWER LEFT forecourt opposite the café. The player will approach from the RIGHT. Show a small worn neighborhood newsstand in slightly elevated three-quarter view, with the main broad open service window facing down/right toward the viewer, a narrow left side wall, and a substantial but shallow slate-blue sheet-metal roof. Low blue-gray wooden counter, dusty teal panels, a few tidy newspaper stacks and muted plum/cream publications in two simple racks. Use large readable shapes, individually placed crisp pixel clusters and charcoal outlines, same pixel texture as the café. At game scale the booth should be about 1.7 times the height of the player and 3 times her width. Avoid a toy shop or tiny vending-machine look.
The vendor is NOT a man or a figure wearing anything. It is an opaque near-black SHADOW: one oddly asymmetric soft organic silhouette, like a patch of living darkness rising from the interior behind the counter. No hood, cowl, robe, coat, hat, human shoulders, face, eyes, mouth, skin, skeletal features, skull, fingers, arms or hands. Its upper outline is a broad rounded irregular shape with one gently tapering sideways tip, nothing like a hood opening. Its body merges into the dark interior under the counter. Make its silhouette clearly readable against the lighter slate-gray back wall, using only a very restrained dusty violet edge, no luminous outline. Quietly uncanny, still, shapeless; do not turn it into a cute ghost, a grim reaper or smoke particles.
17:40 aesthetic: cold afternoon blues, muted periwinkle highlights, dusty violet shadows, weathered gray paper, low saturation. One tiny warm reflection on paper is enough; NO interior orange lamp or large orange glow. Fascia text exactly "JORNAIS", hand-painted off-white simple pixel capitals, small and readable. The rest of the publications have abstract cover blocks without text.
Framing: the complete kiosk, roof, side racks, counter and base, generous transparent margins. No street scene, ground platform, pavement, background, contact shadow, border or watermark. True alpha transparency. One kiosk and its ONE formless shadow inhabitant inside. No person outside. Logical artwork approximately 140 by 140 pixels enlarged in consistent square pixel clusters.
